title: The Keeper of Gull Point
summary: Abel Crane, keeper of the Gull Point light, was found dead in the lamp room at 9pm, struck with a brass spanner. A storm had cut the point off from the village, and four people were sheltering there.

victim.name: Abel Crane
victim.description: The old keeper, who had written to the harbour board about the light's failing inspections.

suspects.name: Jory Penhale
suspects.description: The assistant keeper, young, broke, and often down at the boathouse after dark.

suspects.name: Nell Trask
suspects.description: A fisherwoman who tied up at the jetty to wait out the storm.

suspects.name: Mr. Quill
suspects.description: The harbour board's inspector, who signed the light's last three safety reports.

suspects.name: Ada Vos
suspects.description: A painter renting the keeper's spare cottage for the season.

planned_lies.says: By nine I was in the cottage drying off by the stove. I had finished with the lamp hours before.
I was in the cottage at nine, same as everyone with any sense.

clues.description: Nell Trask was at the jetty at 9pm, doubling the lines on her boat.
At 9pm Ada Vos saw Nell Trask by lantern light and helped her with a rope.
The boathouse ledger has Jory Penhale logging a crate at 9:05pm.
The lamp room log has an entry in Mr. Quill's hand timed 9pm.
Jory Penhale lent Mr. Quill the brass spanner that afternoon.
Nell Trask heard the keeper tell Jory his debt was overdue.
At 8pm Nell Trask passed Mr. Quill on the way up from the jetty.

documents.title: Boathouse ledger
documents.body: Crates in, Thursday. 9:05pm, one crate, no markings, received J.P. Storm rising, tide high at ten.

documents.title: Lamp room log
documents.body: 21:00. Lens turned and checked, mechanism sound. Inspection passed. Signed, H. Quill, harbour board.

documents.title: Tide table for Gull Point
documents.body: Thursday. High water 21:58, height 5.1 metres. Low water 04:10. Spring tides; gale warning in force.

documents.title: Coastguard storm bulletin
documents.body: Storm signal raised at 16:00. Wind north-west, rising to force 9 by evening. The causeway to Gull Point impassable from 18:00 until the morning ebb.

documents.title: Lease for the spare cottage
documents.body: Received of Miss A. Vos, rent for the spare cottage, May to September, eight pounds. No oils or turpentine to be stored near the lamp room stairs. A. Crane, keeper.

documents.title: Page from Ada Vos's sketchbook
documents.body: Study of the point under storm cloud, grey on grey. The beam comes round every ten seconds and turns the rain to silver. Try again in oils if the weather holds.

documents.title: Fish sale receipt
documents.body: Polwenna quay, Wednesday. Forty mackerel, two crab. Sold by N. Trask. Paid in full.

documents.title: Keeper's stores
documents.body: Paraffin, forty gallons. Wicks, two dozen. Mantles, one box. Chimney glasses, six. Mineral oil for the clockwork, two tins.

documents.title: Pawn ticket
documents.body: Polwenna Loan Office. Pledged: one silver watch, engraved. Lent: fifteen shillings. Name: J. Penhale. Redeem within three months.

documents.title: Clipping from the Polwenna Gazette
documents.body: The fishing fleet stayed in harbour on Thursday as the worst gale of the year came ashore. The causeway road to Gull Point was closed by the coastguard.

documents.title: Harbour board circular
documents.body: To all keepers. From the first of the month, log entries are to be made in ink, with the hour in the twenty-four hour clock, and signed in full.

documents.title: Postcard from Ada Vos
documents.body: Dear Bea, the keeper is a gruff old thing but feeds me fish. Painting the cliffs every day; the light here is wonderful. Home in September. Love, A.

documents.title: Notice on the boathouse door
documents.body: No crates to be stored here without the keeper's mark. No lamps left lit. By order, A. Crane, keeper.

documents.title: Constable's report
documents.body: Telephone line to the point down in the storm. Reached Gull Point by boat at first light. Keeper found dead in the lamp room, struck once on the head. Four persons sheltering at the point detained for questioning.

documents.title: Letter from the harbour board
documents.body: Dear Mr. Crane, the Board acknowledges your letter of the 3rd concerning the Gull Point light. An inspector will attend on Thursday.

documents.title: Keeper's letter to the harbour board
documents.body: Sirs, I must again report that the Gull Point light failed twice this winter, for near an hour each time. The inspection reports say otherwise. I ask the Board to send a second man to see for himself.

documents.title: Chandlery invoice
documents.body: Polwenna Chandlery. To N. Trask: two coils manila rope, one tin Stockholm tar, a dozen shackles. Account overdue, kindly settle.
